name: Jerome Powell
role: Fed Governor (returns to Governor seat Jan 2028; Chair term expired May 15, 2026 — succeeded by Kevin Warsh)
quote: The tariff effects will include higher inflation and slower growth — significantly larger than anticipated. We are well positioned to wait for greater clarity before adjusting policy. [Harvard, Mar 30 2026]. LEGACY: Powell's Chair term expired May 15, 2026. His 8-year tenure: cut rates from 23-year high 5.50% to 3.50-3.75% across 175 bps of easing; navigated post-COVID 9.1% inflation back to ~3%; avoided NBER-declared recession through Iran war energy shock. Final handoff: CPI 3.8% (May 12) + PPI 6.0% (May 13) — inflation unsolved. Warsh inherits the stagflation trap.

name: Christine Lagarde
role: President, European Central Bank (term through 2027) — Delivered June 11 Hike to 2.25%
quote: The volatility we have seen in global markets this week is a direct consequence of trade policy uncertainty. [Apr 4, 2026]. JUNE 11 DECISION: The ECB Governing Council raised all three key rates 25bp — deposit facility to 2.25%, main refi to 2.40%, marginal lending to 2.65% — the first hike since July 2023, reversing the final step of the prior 8-cut easing cycle. New staff projections showed HICP inflation at 3.0% (2026), 2.3% (2027), and 2.0% (2028), with growth cut to 0.8%/1.2%/1.5%. Lagarde cited Iran-war-driven energy inflation as the primary driver and left the door open to further tightening depending on incoming data.

name: Scott Bessent
role: US Treasury Secretary — Post-Summit Trade Architecture; Section 122 Tariff Legal Battle Active
quote: The market selloff is an adjustment to a structurally stronger American economy. Short-term volatility is the price of restoring American manufacturing competitiveness and ending decades of unfair trade practices. We are building something durable. [Apr 6, 2026]. STATUS May 17: Section 122 tariff legal status — CIT struck down Section 122 (May 7, 2-1); Federal Circuit stay issued May 12; tariffs still collected. Bessent and USTR Greer coordinating response; Section 301 authority likely contingency. USTR Greer (May 17): US can restore 'Busan Deal' ~41.6% China tariff level. Section 122 cliff July 23 (66 days) — Congressional extension vs Section 301 pivot are the two options. Post-summit: Board of Trade framework established; $30B from each side (framework only); Greer confirmed bilateral trade/investment boards are now formalized for the first time.

name: Jamieson Greer
role: US Trade Representative — Canada Talks Collapsed Aug 21; Section 338 Tariffs Live; Canada Retaliation Effective Sept 8
quote: We have never had a Board of Trade or a Board of Investment before, we've always had an ad hoc approach. [CBS Face the Nation, May 17, 2026]. The Chinese know that the United States can elevate tariffs to the higher level that we had at the time of what we call the Busan deal in October. [CBS Face the Nation, May 17, 2026]. STATUS AUG 25: Talks between Greer and Canadian Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc collapsed late Aug 21 after their fourth meeting in three weeks failed to resolve differences over auto-content rules, steel/aluminum tariffs, and dairy supply management. The Section 338 tariffs (50% on ~$20B of Canadian autos, alcohol, and dairy) took effect Aug 22, three days after their original Aug 19 date following a brief suspension. Prime Minister Carney declared Canada 'at war' with the US on trade and, on Aug 25, announced tiered 15/25/50% retaliatory tariffs on ~$20B of US goods effective Sept 8, plus a C$7.5B support package. Trump escalated further Aug 24, threatening 50% tariffs on Canadian autos, auto parts, and steel from Jan 1, 2027 — clouding the USMCA's scheduled 2026 joint review. STATUS May 17: Greer is the architect of the post-Trump-Xi summit trade architecture — the Board of Trade, Board of Investment, and $30B-for-$30B tariff reduction framework, alongside the standing Busan Deal threat to restore China's tariff rate toward ~41.6% if Beijing does not engage constructively.

name: Kristalina Georgieva
role: Managing Director, IMF (2nd term from Oct 2024)
quote: Our April 2026 WEO confirms global growth at 3.1% in our reference scenario — with an adverse scenario of 2.5% and severe scenario of 2.0% if the conflict continues. Headline inflation has risen to 4.4% globally. The IMF is providing $20-50 billion in emergency support to energy-importing developing economies. We call on all countries to coordinate on debt restructuring, quota reform, and to resist the fragmentation of the global trading system. [IMF Spring Meetings closing, Apr 18 2026]

name: Li Qiang
role: Premier, People's Republic of China (since March 2023)
quote: China's manufacturing PMI returning to expansion in March confirms the resilience of our economy. We are committed to working constructively with the United States on trade, rare earths, and shared economic stability. A stable bilateral relationship benefits all.

name: Kazuo Ueda
role: Governor, Bank of Japan (since April 2023) — Delivered June 16 Hike to 1.00%, Highest Since 1995
quote: We will continue our efforts to achieve the price stability target in a sustainable and stable manner. [Apr 28 2026]. JUNE 16 DECISION: The BOJ raised its overnight call rate 25bp to 1.00% — the highest level since 1995 — in a 7-1 vote (Asada dissenting), citing Iran-war-driven energy-cost pass-through risk. The hike landed the same day Warsh's first FOMC opened, reviving August-2024 carry-unwind fears; the immediate reaction was orderly (Nikkei +0.46%), but the yen still fell to a fresh ~40-year low past 162/USD by June 30 despite the hike and an estimated $72.5bn in prior BOJ/MOF FX intervention — underscoring that yen weakness remains unresolved.

name: Andrew Bailey
role: Governor, Bank of England (term through 2030) — Apr 30: Held 3.75% (8-1), one hawkish dissenter
quote: This is the most difficult combination of economic effects we have faced since I became Governor. Energy prices from the Middle East conflict are very uncertain but likely to have a long-lived effect. In a worst-case scenario, rates could need to return to 5.25% and inflation could spike to 6.2%. Monetary policy cannot influence energy prices — our tools address demand, not supply shocks. [Apr 30 2026 post-decision]. DECISION Apr 30: MPC voted 8-1 to hold Bank Rate at 3.75%. One dissenting member called for immediate +25bp hike to 4.00% — most hawkish single dissent in this cycle. UK CPI 3.3% (March); IMF downgraded UK 2026 growth to 0.8%. Next MPC meeting: June 18, 2026.

name: Ajay Banga
quote: Developing countries are facing a convergence of challenges — high debt, elevated food and energy costs, and now trade disruption. The World Bank stands ready to support resilient and inclusive growth.

name: Pan Gongsheng
role: Governor, People's Bank of China (since July 2023)
quote: The People's Bank of China will strengthen counter-cyclical adjustment, maintain liquidity at reasonably ample levels, and support the real economy. We have ample tools to deal with external shocks.

name: Gita Gopinath
role: First Deputy Managing Director, IMF; former Chief Economist
quote: Trade fragmentation is a significant drag on long-run productivity and growth. Economies that become more closed lose the gains from specialization and economies of scale that have underpinned decades of prosperity.

name: Christopher Waller
role: Federal Reserve Governor; dissented for rate cut at Jan 2026 FOMC
quote: I believe the policy rate is still meaningfully restrictive and that we can gradually lower it. The risks to achieving our dual-mandate goals are more balanced than our current stance reflects.

name: Isabel Schnabel
role: Executive Board Member, ECB (Germany); inflation hawk
quote: We should not be complacent about inflation persistence. While disinflation has made significant progress, wage growth and services inflation require us to remain vigilant. Cutting too aggressively risks undoing years of credibility-building.

name: Donald Trump
role: US President — Canada Trade War Live: Section 338 Tariffs in Effect, 2027 Auto-Tariff Threat Issued Aug 24
quote: Build in the U.S. and there are ZERO TARIFFS. [Truth Social, Aug 24, 2026, threatening 50% tariffs on Canadian autos, auto parts, and steel effective Jan 1, 2027, and calling Canada 'among the worst Nations in the World to deal with']. STATUS AUG 25: After US-Canada trade talks collapsed Aug 21, Trump's Section 338 tariffs (50% on ~$20B of Canadian autos, alcohol, and dairy) took effect Aug 22. Canada responded Aug 25 with tiered 15-50% retaliatory tariffs on ~$20B of US goods, effective Sept 8. Trump's Aug 24 threat to raise Canadian auto/steel tariffs to 50% from Jan 1, 2027 further clouds the USMCA's scheduled 2026 joint review; GM and Ford shares fell 1-3% on the announcement. PRIOR: JUNE 15-17 — Trump announced a US-Iran deal framework (June 15), triggering a global equity rally; the MOU was formally signed June 17, with Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and the US lifting its naval blockade. The MOU's 60-day window expired Aug 17 without a permanent deal. STATUS AUG 10: The Section 122 tariff cliff resolved on schedule July 24 — Section 301 forced-labor tariffs (10-12.5%, 60 economies) took effect without a Congressional extension.

name: Janet Yellen
role: Former US Treasury Secretary (Jan 2021–Jan 2025); Former Fed Chair
quote: We achieved something rare in economic history: bringing inflation down from 40-year highs without triggering a recession. The soft landing was not guaranteed — it required skill, patience, and some good fortune with supply chains.

name: François Villeroy de Galhau
role: Governor, Banque de France; ECB Governing Council dove
quote: The eurozone cannot afford complacency in the face of tariff-driven stagnation. With inflation near target, the ECB must prioritize economic momentum. Europe needs its own fiscal tools to complement monetary easing.

name: Philip Jefferson
quote: Energy prices are a key source of uncertainty in the current inflation outlook. Sustained increases in oil prices could temporarily push up inflation and complicate our path back to the 2% target. We are monitoring developments carefully. [Mar 26, 2026]

name: Austan Goolsbee
role: President, Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago (since Jan 2023)
quote: Stagflation is the worst situation for the central bank because raising rates doesn't solve it, cutting rates doesn't solve it, and staying the same doesn't solve it. The longer this goes where we never got to see the decrease in inflation, that starts pushing rate cuts out of '26 — potentially into 2027. [Semafor World Economy 2026 Conference, Apr 14, 2026]

name: Kevin Warsh
role: 17th Federal Reserve Chair — Jackson Hole Debut Keynote Aug 28; Next FOMC Sept 16-17
quote: I will act with independence and resolve in the public interest. [Swearing-in ceremony, White House, May 22, 2026]. THE FIRST FOMC (June 16-17): Warsh's inaugural meeting as Chair unanimously held the fed funds rate at 3.50-3.75%. His Summary of Economic Projections turned hawkish: the 2026 median dot rose to 3.8% from 3.4% in March — implying a hike, not a cut — with 9 of 18 members projecting at least one 2026 hike. Warsh declined to submit his own dot, calling the tool 'inconsistent with his views,' and cut the post-meeting statement to roughly 130 words (from 341 in April) — a marked communication-style shift. The meeting landed the same day as the BOJ's hike to 1.00% and the signed US-Iran MOU, which crashed Brent ~11% and partially offset the hawkish signal. Subsequent data — May PCE hot at 4.1% (Jun 25), weak June jobs (+57K, Jul 2), and June CPI cooling to 3.5% (Jul 14) — has left the rate path genuinely uncertain heading into the July 28-29 FOMC, a non-SEP meeting where consensus expects another hold. JULY 28-29 FOMC: Despite the July 23 Hormuz/Red Sea oil shock pushing September hike odds to ~82%, Warsh's FOMC held rates at 3.50-3.75%. Three members dissented in favor of a hike — an unusually large hawkish bloc. Warsh called the internal disagreement a 'good family fight,' and when asked whether the decision amounted to a 'pause,' said he would not characterize it that way. The subsequent Aug 7 jobs report (NFP -23K, a sharp miss with -103K combined May/June revisions) reversed the hawkish repricing heading into the September meeting. JACKSON HOLE (Aug 27-29): The Kansas City Fed's symposium ('Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy') opened Aug 27 with jobless claims falling to 203K, setting up Warsh's first keynote as Chair on Aug 28 at 10am ET. Boston Fed's Susan Collins said Aug 25 that rates 'need to rise soon' absent evidence of sustained disinflation — one of several regional presidents pushing a hawkish line into the symposium. Warsh is expected to avoid explicit forward guidance, but traders are watching for any signal on whether he views 2026's re-accelerated inflation as transitory ahead of the Sept 16-17 FOMC.
